The Prophet forgot the date of the Night of Qadr when two men quarrelled, and said to seek it on the seventh, ninth or fifth of Ramadan's last ten nights.
The Prophet sought the Night of Qadr in Itikaf, said it lies in the odd nights of the last ten, and his dream of prostrating in mud came true.
Praying on the Night of Qadr forgives past sins; it is sought in odd nights of Ramadan's last ten, its date withheld over a quarrel; the Prophet strove hard then.
Abu al-Khair, emigrating from Yemen, hears the Prophet was buried five days before, and learns Bilal said the Night of Qadr is one of seven nights in the last ten.
The Prophet came to tell the date of the Night of Qadr, but two men quarrelled and its knowledge was taken away; seek it on the ninth, seventh or fifth.
Some were shown the Night of Qadr in the last seven days of Ramadan, and the Prophet said to seek it then.
